props.gloss_en: the baraita: the festival peace-offering and all the time of the festival peace-offering -- one postpones
the stam: 'chagigah' is clear -- if the festival falls on Shabbat it is postponed to after Shabbat
Rav Oshaya: this is what it says -- chagigah [is postponed] on Shabbat, and the burnt-offering of appearance even on yom tov, which is the time of chagigah
the stam: whose view is it [on Rav Oshaya's reading]? Beit Shammai's
Beit Shammai: one brings peace-offerings on yom tov and does not lean on them
Beit Shammai: but not burnt-offerings
Beit Hillel: one brings peace-offerings and burnt-offerings
Beit Hillel: and one leans on them
Rava: chagigah is postponed throughout the time of chagigah, and no further
Mishnah Chagigah: one who did not offer the festival offering on the first day of the festival offers it throughout the festival, and on its last day
...if the festival passed and he did not offer, he is not liable for it
Rav Ashi: chagigah and all the time of chagigah is postponed -- even Atzeret, which is one day, is postponed
Mishnah Chagigah: they concede that if Atzeret falls on Shabbat, the day of slaughter is after Shabbat
Rebbi planted a sapling on Purim
and he bathed in [the time of] the wagons of Tzippori on the seventeenth of Tammuz
and he sought to abolish the Ninth of Av -- and they did not agree with him
R' Abba bar Zavda: it was not so; it was a Ninth of Av that fell on Shabbat and was deferred to after Shabbat, and Rebbi said: since it was deferred, let it be deferred -- and the Sages did not agree
he read of him: 'two are better than one' (Eccl 4:9)
Rav Yosef on Esther 9:19: 'gladness' teaches that eulogy is forbidden [on Purim]
'feasting' teaches that fasting is forbidden
'and a good day [yom tov]' teaches that labour is forbidden
answer 1: Rebbi kept the fourteenth, and he planted on the fifteenth
Rebbi was in Tiberias, and Tiberias was walled from the days of Joshua son of Nun
answer 2: Rebbi kept the fifteenth, and when he planted it was on the fourteenth
Chizkiya read [the Megillah] in Tiberias on the fourteenth and on the fifteenth
he was in doubt whether it was walled from the days of Joshua son of Nun or not
Megillat Ta'anit: the fourteenth and the fifteenth are days of Purim, on which one may not eulogise
Rava: [the scroll's listing both days] is needed only to forbid those of this day on that day, and those of that day on this day
answer: that is so for eulogy and fasting; but labour -- one day and no more
Rav saw a certain man sowing flax on Purim and cursed him, and his flax did not grow
Rabba breih deRava: even if you say [Rebbi planted] on his own day -- eulogy and fasting they accepted upon themselves, labour they did not accept upon themselves
for at first is written 'gladness and feasting and a good day' (Esther 9:19), and at the end 'to make them days of feasting and gladness' (Esther 9:22), and 'good day' is not written
answer: it was a matter permitted that others practised as forbidden; and in Rebbi's place it was not the custom
or say: it actually was the custom, and Rebbi planted a planting of joy
Mishnah Ta'anit: if these [fasts] passed and they were not answered, one decreases trade, building and planting, betrothals and marriages
the baraita on it: 'building' is building of joy, 'planting' is planting of joy; building of joy is one who builds a wedding-house for his son; planting of joy is one who plants an avurneki of kings
'and the fortified cities: Ziddim, Zer, and Chamat, Rakkat and Kinneret' (Josh 19:35), and we hold that Rakkat is Tiberias
answer: this is why he was in doubt -- on one side its wall was the sea
the baraita: 'which has a wall' (Lev 25:30) -- and not a wall of roofs
'round about' (Lev 25:31) -- excluding Tiberias, whose sea is its wall

answer: regarding houses of walled cities he had no doubt; his doubt was regarding the Megillah reading -- are the unwalled and the walled distinguished because these are exposed and those not (and this one too is exposed), or because these are protected and those not (and this one too is protected)?
Rav Asi read the Megillah in Huzal on the fourteenth and on the fifteenth
he was in doubt whether it was walled from the days of Joshua son of Nun or not
some say Rav Asi said: this Huzal of the house of Binyamin is walled from the days of Joshua
R' Yochanan: when I was a child I said something that I asked the elders about, and it was found as I said
Chamat is Tiberias
it is called Chamat on account of the hot springs of Tiberias
Rakkat is Tzippori
it is called Rakkat because it is raised like the bank of a river
Kinneret is Ginosar
it is called Kinneret because its fruit are sweet as the sound of harps

when a man dies here, there they eulogise him: 'great was he in Sheshakh, and he had a name in Rakkat'; and when they bring the coffin up there: 'lovers of the remnant, dwellers of Rakkat, go out and receive the slain of the deep'
the eulogy for R' Zeira: the land of Shinar conceived and bore, the land of the deer raised her delights; 'woe to her', said Rakkat, 'for she has lost her precious vessel'
rather, Rabbah: Chamat is the hot springs of Gerar
it is called Rakkat because even the empty ones in it are full of mitzvot as a pomegranate
Rakkat is its [Tiberias's] name
R' Yirmeya: it is called Tiberias because it sits at the navel of the Land of Israel
Rava: it is called Tiberias because its sight is good
Zeira: Kitron is Tzippori
it is called Tzippori because it sits on a mountaintop like a bird
Kitron was in Zevulun's portion, as written: 'Zevulun did not drive out the inhabitants of Kitron or of Nahalol' (Judg 1:30)
and Zevulun resented his portion, as stated 'Zevulun is a people that scorned its life to die' (Judg 5:18) -- why? because 'Naftali is on the heights of the field'
Zevulun before the Holy One: to my brothers You gave fields and vineyards and to me mountains and hills; to my brothers lands, and to me seas and rivers
He said to him: all will need you for the chilazon, as stated 'they shall call peoples to the mountain... and the hidden treasures of the sand' (Deut 33:19)
Rav Yosef teaches: 'treasures' -- this is the chilazon
'hidden' -- this is the tarit
'sand' -- this is white glass
he [Zevulun] said before Him: Master of the world, who will inform me?
He said to him: 'there they shall offer sacrifices of righteousness' -- let this be your sign: whoever takes from you without payment will not prosper in his trade at all
if you think Kitron is Tzippori, why did Zevulun resent his portion? Tzippori is a thing far superior
Reish Lakish: I myself saw the [land] flowing with milk and honey of Tzippori, and it was sixteen mil by sixteen mil
R' Yochanan: I myself saw the [land] flowing with milk and honey of all the Land of Israel, and it was from Bei Kovei to the fortress of Tulbakni, twenty-two parsa long and six parsa wide
answer: even so, fields and vineyards were preferable to him
'and Ekron shall be uprooted' (Zeph 2:4) -- this is Caesarea, daughter of Edom
R' Abbahu: it sits among the sands, and it was a stake stuck in Israel in the days of the Greeks; when the Hasmonean kingdom prevailed and defeated them, they called it 'the captured tower of Shir'
R' Yosei bar Chanina on Zech 9:7: 'I will remove his blood from his mouth' -- this is their house of altars
'and his detestations from between his teeth' -- this is their house of piles
'and he too shall remain for our God' -- these are the synagogues and study halls in Edom
'and he shall be as a chief in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite' -- these are the theatres and circuses in Edom, where the officers of Judah are destined to teach Torah in public
R' Yitzchak: Leshem is Pamyas
R' Yitzchak: it [Caesarea] was a metropolis of kings
some say: [metropolis of kings] -- kings are raised in it
and some say: kings are appointed from it

Caesarea and Jerusalem: if a man tells you both are destroyed, do not believe; both settled, do not believe; Caesarea destroyed and Jerusalem settled, or Jerusalem destroyed and Caesarea settled -- believe
as stated 'I shall be filled, she is laid waste' (Ezek 26:2): if this one is full, that one is waste
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: from here -- 'and one people shall be stronger than the other' (Gen 25:23)
Isaac before the Holy One: Master of the world, let favour be shown to Esau ... [answered 'he is wicked'] Isaac said: 'he has not learned righteousness' (Isa 26:10)
He said to him: he is wicked; ... 'in the land of uprightness he will deal wrongfully'
Isaac said: if so, 'let him not behold the majesty of the Lord'
Jacob before the Holy One: Master of the world, do not grant the wicked Esau his heart's desire (Ps 140:9)
'do not further his device' -- this is Germamya of Edom, who, were they to go forth, would destroy the whole world

R' Chama bar Chanina: there are three hundred crowned princes in Germamya of Edom and three hundred sixty-five chieftains in Rome; each day these go out against those, one of them is killed, and they are busied appointing a king
R' Yitzchak: if a man says 'I toiled and did not find', do not believe; 'I did not toil and found', do not believe; 'I toiled and found', believe
the stam: that holds in words of Torah; in trade it is help from Heaven
and in words of Torah we said it only of sharpening; but to retain learning it is help from Heaven
R' Yitzchak: if you see a wicked man on whom the hour smiles, do not provoke him
as stated: 'do not contend with evildoers' (Ps 37:1)
and not only that, but his ways prosper
as stated: 'his ways prosper at all times' (Ps 10:5)
and not only that, but he prevails in judgment
as stated: 'Your judgments are far above, out of his sight' (Ps 10:5)
and not only that, but he sees [the downfall of] his enemies
as stated: 'as for all his adversaries, he snorts at them' (Ps 10:5)
it is permitted to provoke the wicked in this world
as stated: 'those who forsake the Torah praise the wicked, but those who keep the Torah contend with them' (Prov 28:4)
and if a man whispers to you: 'do not contend with evildoers, do not envy the workers of iniquity' (Ps 37:1)
R' Dostai: rather, 'do not contend with evildoers' -- to be like evildoers; 'do not envy the workers of iniquity' -- to be like the workers of iniquity
and it says: 'let not your heart envy sinners' (Prov 23:17)
answer 1: no difficulty -- this [the warning] concerns his own affairs, that [the permission] matters of Heaven
answer 2: both concern his own affairs -- this of a completely righteous man, that of one not completely righteous
Rav Huna on Hab 1:13: 'the wicked swallows one more righteous than he' -- one [merely] more righteous than he he swallows; a completely righteous man he does not swallow
answer 3: when the hour smiles on him it is different

objections.gloss_en: רבי, לא כך היה מעשה -- it was a deferred Ninth of Av, and Rebbi sought only that it be deferred altogether (טובים השנים: the correction stands)
ורבי היכי נטע נטיעה בפורים? והתני רב יוסף: ...ויום טוב -- מלמד שאסור בעשיית מלאכה

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא: רבי בר חמיסר הוה, וכי נטע בארביסר הוה (= p_okimta_bar_chamesar; the first answer, bar arbeisar, was retracted)
אפילו תימא ביומיה -- labour they did not accept upon themselves (= p_lo_kiblu_melacha)

objections.gloss_en: איני? והא רבי בטבריא הוה, וטבריא מוקפת חומה מימות יהושע בן נון -- Rebbi kept the fifteenth
ומי פשיטא ליה דטבריא מוקפת חומה מימות יהושע בן נון? והא חזקיה קרי בטבריא בארביסר ובחמיסר

answered_by.gloss_en: לחזקיה מספקא ליה, לרבי פשיטא ליה

objections.gloss_en: וכי פשיטא ליה, מי שרי? והכתיב במגילת תענית... דלא למספד בהון, ואמר רבא: לא נצרכא אלא לאסור את של זה בזה (kind tanya: a tannaitic scroll; no kind names והכתיב במגילת תענית)

answered_by.gloss_en: הני מילי בהספד ובתענית, אבל מלאכה -- יום אחד ותו לא (= p_melacha_yom_echad)

objections.gloss_en: איני? והא רב חזייה לההוא גברא דהוה קא שדי כיתנא בפוריא ולטייה

answered_by.gloss_en: התם בר יומא הוה -- there it was the man's own day

objections.gloss_en: ואלא רב מאי טעמא לטייה לההוא גברא? -- if labour was never accepted, why the curse?

answered_by.gloss_en: דברים המותרין ואחרים נהגו בהן איסור הוה, ובאתריה דרבי לא נהוג (= p_devarim_hamutarin)
ואיבעית אימא: לעולם נהוג, ורבי נטיעה של שמחה נטע (= p_netia_shel_simcha)

objections.gloss_en: ומי מספקא ליה מילתא דטבריא? והכתיב וערי מבצר... רקת, וקיימא לן רקת זו טבריא (kind svara: a verse with a held identification; no kind names it)

answered_by.gloss_en: משום דחד גיסא שורא דימא הוה (= p_shura_deyama)

objections.gloss_en: אי הכי, אמאי מספקא ליה? ודאי לאו חומה היא! דתניא: ...סביב -- פרט לטבריא שימה חומתה

answered_by.gloss_en: לענין בתי ערי חומה לא מספקא ליה; כי קא מספקא ליה לענין מקרא מגילה (= p_safek_mikra_megillah)

objections.gloss_en: מי איכא למאן דאמר רקת לאו טבריא היא? והא כי שכיב איניש הכא התם ספדי ליה הכי: ...ושם לו ברקת
כי נח נפשיה דרבי זירא פתח עליה ההוא ספדנא: ...אוי נא לה, אמרה רקת

וקטרון ציפורי היא? והא קטרון בחלקו של זבולון הואי... וזבולון מתרעם על מדותיו הוה... ואי סלקא דעתך קטרון זו ציפורי, אמאי מתרעם? (6a.9) -- with two וכי תימא pre-emptions refuted by Reish Lakish and R' Yochanan (supports below)

answered_by.gloss_en: אפילו הכי, שדות וכרמים עדיפא ליה (= p_sadot_uchramim_adifa)

objections.gloss_en: ואם לחשך אדם לומר: אל תתחר במרעים ואל תקנא בעושי עולה

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא: אל תתחר במרעים -- להיות כמרעים (= p_al_titchar_lihyot)

objections.gloss_en: איני? והאמר רבי יוחנן משום רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: מותר להתגרות ברשעים בעולם הזה (kind svara under protest: no ObjectionKind names an amoraic-memra contradiction)
